drivingQuestion: When may one pass through a synagogue as a shortcut?
outcomeNote: Two amoraic qualifications are appended to the synagogue rule without challenge.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: אִם הָיָה שְׁבִיל מֵעִיקָּרוֹ — מוּתָּר. אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הַנִּכְנָס לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת לְהִתְפַּלֵּל, מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ קַפֶּנְדַּרְיָא. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְבֹא עַם הָאָרֶץ לִפְנֵי ה׳ בַּמּוֹעֲדִים וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rabbi Abbahu said: If it was originally a path» that passed through the site where the synagogue was erected, «one is permitted» to pass through, as the public right of passage is not negated by the construction of a synagogue. «Rabbi Ḥelbo said» that «Rav Huna said: One who enters a synagogue to pray is permitted to make it a shortcut, as it is stated: “But when the people of the land shall come before the Lord in the appointed seasons,» he that enters by way of the north gate to worship shall go forth by the way of the south gate” (Ezekiel 46:9).

moves.cueHe: רבי אבהו אמר: אם היה שביל מעיקרו
moves.summary: R' Abbahu qualifies the synagogue shortcut prohibition of the previous unit for a pre-existing path
moves.about: whether the prohibition of using a synagogue as a shortcut applies where a public path already ran through the site

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חלבו אמר רב הונא
moves.summary: in Rav Huna's name: one who entered to pray may make it a shortcut
moves.about: Ezekiel's rule that one entering by the north gate goes out by the south gate is the prooftext

moves.summary: Ezekiel 46:9, on entering by one gate and leaving by another, is brought as proof
moves.about: R' Ḥelbo reports Rav Huna's permission for one who entered a synagogue in order to pray

edges.cueHe: רבי אבהו אמר: אם היה שביל מעיקרו — מותר
edges.about: whether the prohibition of using a synagogue as a shortcut applies where a public path already ran through the site
